fixer.summary:
T-22 is fixed: Bless now refuses a non-creature target cleanly instead of crashing. The cause was that `_as_list` keeps a name that isn't a creature (here "door") as a plain string, and `_bless` then crashed on `t.name`. I added the check to the existing `_target_cap` in `dungdra/spells.py`. It already runs before anything is spent and only applies to spells with a target cap. Every such spell (bless, command, hold person, aid, invisibility) targets creatures, so any target that isn't a creature (no `id`) is now refused, with page=sd["page"] and rule=SPELL.bless#6 for Bless, or the spell's own rule for the others. The code is tagged SRD[SPELL.bless#6].

Checks:
- `test_bless_cant_target_an_object` passes with `--runxfail`. Without that flag it shows as XPASS(strict), the only failure in tests/srd and tests/scenarios, which goes away once the harness removes the marker.
- Unit tests: 264 passed.
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` are clean, and dev-gate passes.

One other test in tests/srd/test_spells.py fails under `--runxfail`: `test_bless_adds_1d4_to_a_death_saving_throw`. It belongs to T-23 (death saves don't pick up Bless's 1d4) and is still correctly marked xfail; this change doesn't affect it.

followups.title: Spell target kind as data: add a field such as `targets="creature"` to the spell data and check it in one place in cast(). Today the 'targets creatures' refusal sits inside _target_cap, so only spells with max_targets (bless, command, hold person, aid, invisibility) refuse an object. Creature-only spells without a cap accept one silently.

review.summary: The fix is sound. Bless now refuses a non-creature target inside _target_cap. That check runs before the slot is spent or Concentration starts, and the refusal carries page=113 and rule=SPELL.bless#6. It tells creatures from other targets with `hasattr(t, "id")`, the test the codebase already uses for this (cast's Total Cover check, game.get). The non-creature check covers every spell that has max_targets: command, hold person, aid and invisibility. All of these target creatures in the SRD, so this applies the rule generally rather than special-casing Bless. A refactor follow-up suggests storing the target kind as its own data field instead of tying it to the cap. The strict xfail on the acceptance test was removed correctly. The new unit test checks the rule and page, and that no slot is spent, no Concentration starts and nothing is logged. The parametrized test checks that each capped spell cites its own rule and page.
